_doc: Run-wide survivor tuning (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md sections 5, 6; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md 4.4.4). Everything here is tier C (ours / emulator-like) unless a note says otherwise; canonical WZ numbers are never copied here except where noted as a survivor choice of equipment.

exp_curve._formula: Tier C: exp_to_next(L) = round(a + b*L + c*L^2): L1 23, L7 295, L9 447, L29 3635; 980 EXP to reach Lv8, 1794 to Lv10, 39150 to Lv30. Difficulty-overhaul candidate trained only on 1..60 and 2026; canonical EXP table unchanged.

mob_skills._doc: Tier C: enabled boss kits; slow x retains x percent of upgraded speed; defense x adds flat defense; heal restores the canonical x (y unused, no roll); 140 is timed self weapon immunity.

mob_projectiles._tier: tier C: swept body contact radius when the canonical ball has no lt/rb; 320 px/s fallback only when bulletSpeed is absent/nonpositive (Jr. Balrog). Authored positive bulletSpeed keeps its existing conversion.

mob_attacks._doc: Tier C (#76): ordinary (non-boss) mobs use their canonical Mob.wz attackN (damage, range, attackAfter unchanged). interval = seconds of on-screen, fully visible time between one mob's attack starts (WZ has no attack interval; the first wait is 50-100% of it by spawn identity); dmg_mult scales the canonical MADamage/PADamage (default 1.0, unscaled like contact damage; elites also take stages elites.damage_mult). First-pass values chosen before measurement, not tuned (#77).

combat._doc: Tier C (#166/#200): linear projectile pierce decay keeps at least this fraction of its damage; the shipped default is 10%.

player._start: Tier C: survivor starter stats, the v83 Beginner 50 HP / 5 MP and Three Snails rank 1 (owner: keep the v83 opening pool).
player._fortune: Tier C: card-tier odds only; equipment/NX sources are deferred. This is separate from canonical LUK.
player._ap: Tier C: 5 automatic AP per level; assign to the nearest job ancestor's primary stat, redistributing only earned AP when advancing.
player._ap_paths: Tier C (#186): ap_stat and ap_secondary optionally use <job>:<weapon_path> keys, checked before that job's plain key at each lineage step. A branch row wins over its ancestor's path row. Pirate secondary target equals level (knuckle DEX / gun STR); remaining earned AP goes to STR / DEX. Paths are the recorded advancement choice, not the currently held weapon.
player._ap_pirate_branches: Tier C (#189): the second jobs carry plain rows that copy their weapon's first-job path rows (Brawler 510 = 500:knuckle: STR primary, DEX secondary; Gunslinger 520 = 500:gun: DEX primary, STR secondary), so a branch follows its own weapon whichever path the character took at first job: a knuckle-path Gunslinger switches to DEX with an STR secondary, and the Lv 30 Prime Hands / Cold Mind requirements are met. The branch row wins over the path row (_job_value).
player._ap_warrior: Tier C (spec #151 #163): the Warrior line puts all earned AP into STR and has no ap_secondary entry: none of the 133 weapons and shields in the asset cache whose reqJob is the Warrior bit or any job (Warrior drops, creation weapons, shields) has a reqDEX above 0 (a scan of Character.wz info/reqDEX), so DEX would only be needed once Warrior armour drops exist; add an ap_secondary "100" DEX row with that ticket.
player._ap_secondary: Tier C: per job line, an optional secondary stat that earned AP fills first, up to its base-value target at the character's level (keyframes [{level, target}], linear, floored, held outside their range). The rest goes to ap_stat. Lines without an entry (the Beginner) put all AP into ap_stat. The targets are not in WZ; 200 follows the v83 Magician equipment pattern (reqLUK 15 at Lv13, 30 at Lv28, 40 at Lv38, 70 at Lv68: about level + 2), so the character meets v83 LUK requirements. Second jobs inherit their first job's entry through the job lineage (the same lookup as ap_stat).
player._ap_bowman: Tier C (#166 review, #199/#202/#203): DEX primary; retain STR level+5 through Lv30 and STR35 through Lv34 (including the Lv30/31 QA fixtures), then STR40 at Lv35 and level+5 through Lv70/STR75, held thereafter. Both second jobs inherit this row. Meets every shipped bow/crossbow reqSTR by its canonical reqLevel without equipment bonuses; no general balance tuning.
player._ap_thief: Tier C (#207): LUK primary, DEX secondary target max(25, level): the first-job DEX minimum first, then a modest rising equipment allowance; leaves at least 80 LUK by Lv30 without adding a stat reset. Uses the existing earned-AP redistribution; base creation attributes stay unchanged.
player._equipment: Worn equipment comes from the character (creation outfit, later drops); its stats are the canonical info in the asset cache. weapon_grants, advancing to that job wears this weapon and moves the previous one to the inventory (tier C: Magician 200 gets the Wooden Wand; tier B: Warrior 100 gets the Beginner Warrior's sword 1302077, the v83 instructor's first-job gift, PAD 30, reqLv 10; jobs.json grants.items adds items for the Equip tab). inventory_slots, tier A: a new v83 character's Equip tab.
player._body: Touch hitbox relative to the feet (x, y, w, h), roughly the v83 character's body + head.
player._cast: Targeting measures from cast_height px above the feet; shots start cast_forward px further toward their target (the throwing hand, in front of the body).

growth._int_mp: Tier B: Magician MP growth adds floor(INT / 10), using INT before spending that level's AP.
growth._100: Tier B: Warrior HP 24-28 / MP 4-6 per level (Cosmic levelUp, v83-facts 4), fixed midpoints 26 / 5; Improved MaxHP Increase adds its own HP per level-up on top.
growth._300: Tier B (#199): Bowman HP20-24 / MP14-16 per level, fixed midpoints22/15 (v83-facts4).
growth._400: Tier B (#207): Thief per-level HP 20-24 / MP 14-16, fixed midpoints 22 / 15 (v83-facts 4); existing accumulated-total rounding.
growth._500: Tier B (#186): Pirate per-level HP 22-28 / MP 18-23, fixed midpoints 25 / 20.5 (v83-facts 4). Accumulate fractional growth and round the total as for other jobs.

_level_up_refill: Fraction of the new maximum restored on each level-up, after that level's growth. MP 1.0: tier B, v83 servers refill both pools (Cosmic Character.levelUp calls changeHpMp(maxhp, maxmp)). HP 0.0: tier C, owner choice for difficulty.
_hit_window: Spec #88, tier C (ours): the grace after a landed hit. lengths: the window after the 1st, 2nd, 3rd... chained landed hit, the last held (lengths[0] is the full window, which a boss skill attack always starts). chain_gap: a landed hit this soon (s) after the previous landed hit steps to the next shorter length; after reset_after (s) without a landed hit the chain restarts at lengths[0]; between the two the step holds. Boss skill attacks ignore the window (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md Constants and provenance).
_portals: Same-map portals only: activation box relative to the portal point, lift above arrival before falling, global cooldown in seconds. Tier C: owner choice; source and destination points stay canonical.
_mesos: Meso drops (#107). Per-mob ranges are survivor data in mobs.json ("mesos": [min, max), tier B: v83 server drop data). chance: tier B reference (v83 servers drop a meso entry 40% of the time at rate 1); mult scales every amount, tier C (set once from an estimate: the only Henesys clear in the smoke (random policy, seed 1, 3259 kills, all three bosses) earned 22.9k mesos at mult 1, so 14 gives about 320k, the owner's 300-350k target for a clear (the sensible bot dies at 13-15 min with about 15k at mult 1; see docs/GAME_DESIGN.md 4.2 #107; NX upgrades, #34, may raise it later; it is not tuned further here). boss_drops: tier C, bundles a scheduled boss's death drops, each rolled from its range (bosses always drop, there is no chance roll). fallback: tier C, mobs without a v83 range roll around base + per_level x mob level, low/high x that centre (fitted to the v83 early-roster ranges: level 1 = 4-6, level 22 = 28-42, level 50 = 60-90).
_mob_speed_factor: mob move speed px/s = (speed stat + 100) x this x stage speed (MobKind.SPEED_SCALE is the same 0.625; a different value here rescales every mob)
_mob_motion: tier C: flyer vertical bob amplitude in pixels and period in seconds; pursuit still uses canonical flySpeed through mob_speed_factor
_regen: Tier B: MP recovers in 10-second pulses, base 3 plus every owned skill's `regen` field (skills.json; Improved MP Recovery: floor(character level x skill level / 10), Loadout.regen_bonus). Tier C: always recover 10 HP per pulse; hp_regen/mp_regen modifiers add to each pulse.
_crit: Tier C: every job and damage type, including Beginner, fixed skills and basic attacks, can crit. per_acc is a small untuned placeholder: +0.05 percentage points per ACC. Passive crit damage adds skill-percentage points instead of multiplying (tier B: SouthPerry Critical Shot/Throw).
_pickup: EXP drops: pop speed and sideways spread (px/s), magnet start speed (px/s) and acceleration (px/s^2), live drop cap (the farthest from the player is absorbed into a fresh drop at each new kill), lifetime (s an uncollected drop lies before it expires, its EXP lost; 0 = never) and fade (its last seconds, fading out). They fall with Physics.img gravity/fallSpeed.

bot._engage: Tier C (#162): melee-aware movement. A build whose longest attack (active job-line skills via SkillRunner.reach_of, or the held weapon swing via BasicAttack.reach; Beginner skills only when it has none of its own) reaches less than kite_reach px walks up to the nearest on-level mob within chase_range px and stops at reach_fraction of its longest ready attack, facing it; below retreat_hp of max HP, or while a boss attack winds up, it kites like every other build. Longer-reach builds (every Magician attack reaches 260+) keep the kiting bot unchanged.
bot._doc: Tier C: sensible-policy card scoring. card_scores are base-score overrides keyed by card ID (they replace the BotInput base score, so no current-job bonus is added); they prioritize Guard before learning another attack. gain_step_score is added once per step an offered card grants beyond its first (score = base + gain_step_score * (magnitude - 1); a missing or non-positive magnitude counts as 1, tier names are never special-cased; magnitude is the resolved integer gain). 6 lets a Rare or Epic offer pass the cards just below it, and a Unique stacking card or a Legendary +8 attack rank pass a Normal new attack skill; a clamped offer scores the gain it actually grants (worked numbers beside BotInput.SCORE_GAIN_STEP). Missing entries preserve legacy scoring (Normal cards score exactly the base); the Elixir filler ignores the gain; random card choices remain uniform.
bot._equipment_weights: Tier C (spec #33, #112): how much a bot values each inc* stat of an equipment instance (an item scores the sum of weight x value; stats not listed are worth 0). Keyed by job id ("0" Beginner, "200" Magician; a job uses its own entry, else its nearest ancestor's through the job lineage, so second jobs inherit their first job's); a job line without an entry falls back to the Beginner's. A Magician wants M.ATT, then INT (LUK a little), then defences (M.DEF over W.DEF), then pools and movement. The bot wears the best wearable item per slot at each equipment pickup and level-up (BotInput.auto_equip); BotShop also reads the weights to pick scrolls and to keep or sell spare equipment.
bot._equipment_bowman: Tier C (#199): PAD first, DEX primary and STR secondary; defence/pool/movement weights follow the existing physical baseline, untuned.

_potions: Tier C: starter stock, independent HP/MP drop chances per monster (higher for elites), and bot drink thresholds. Restore amounts come from each current item's canonical spec.

potions._drops: Tier C: normal MP 3% flat, no per-map values (owner, 2026-10-16, #80: level-ups refill MP, so Blues stop piling up); elite MP 60% (#29); stage HP curves tune survival. No starter Blues: the v83 5-MP opening pool cannot hold one.
potions._bot: Tier C: drink only when the missing HP/MP is at least min_restore_fraction of one current potion's canonical restore, with the restore capped at the max HP/MP pool but counted as at least pool_floor of the potion (owner: waste guard for v83-sized pools, so a 5-MP pool never drinks a 100-MP Blue; the cap keeps the 1000-2000 point steps of #229 drinkable, tier C).
potions._schedule: Tier C (ours): automatic potion upgrades by character level (spec #225, replacing the potion-tier cards). Each step {level, kind hp|mp, item} makes the kind's current potion that item once the character reaches the level (sim, at level-up with a notice, and silently on snapshot load); the stock count is kept, a step never downgrades, and an item without a canonical restore spec is skipped. Sorted by level. The first three are the old card gates (Orange @10, Mana Elixir @20, White @25). The next four are researched steps, each tier C (docs/research/v83-potion-progression.md section 6, ticket #229): Unagi 2022003 (1000 HP) and Pure Water 2022000 (800 MP) @40, Ice Cream Pop 2001001 (2000 HP) and Red Bean Sundae 2001002 (2000 MP) @60. The levels are our own reading of thin sources (no source names when players moved to the Lv 60 foods), and the step is job-agnostic, so a small pool wastes the overheal. Restore amounts are never typed here: they come from each item's canonical spec in Item.wz (Consume/0200.img, 0202.img); an old asset cache without these items simply stops at the last tier it holds.

_spawn: SpawnDirector (docs/GAME_DESIGN.md 4): margin outside the view, band of the first spawn ring and band_y, how far it reaches above and below the view (the floors beside the view; -1 = band), min distance to the player, samples per ring, recycle distance (px) and time (s) of the far/unreachable relocation rule, prefer_route (a ring first looks for a point whose NavGraph travel cost to the player is at most half the view width + margin + this many px; -1 = any reachable point), stall_time (s an off-screen mob may go without coming stall_progress px closer by moving itself before it is relocated ahead of the player; 0 = never), trail_margin (px the margin grows on the side the player moves away from: the camera lags about 29 px behind a running player).
_bosses: Tier C: warning/placement/pressure, stalled-pursuit fade relocation, canonical EXP reward multiplier and shower geometry, current-tier potion bundles and bonus choice count; stage entries may override rewards.

rewards._potions: Tier C: halve the MP bundle to 3 for the initial scarcity pass (#37); HP remains 3.

_run_time_cap: Tier C: balance/full-run harness timeout, allowing the finale to continue beyond 15:00.
_nx_award: Tier C placeholders (spec #34 / #115; the balance pass sets them): NX paid at the end of every round. A clear pays clear_bonus[tier] + per_level x levels gained in the round + per_boss x scheduled bosses killed in the round; a death pays the same without the clear bonus. clear_bonus is indexed by the stage's 0-based tier (later tiers reuse the last entry). Deletion, Quit round and tool rounds are never credited.
